learning: If line loss is zero and slalom max_error is below 0.06 m, the spread was the missing piece. If line loss returns at y=0.07 m, the lead is the trigger at this speed, and the spread is not the cure. If slalom steering_oscillation stays above 0.10 with zero line loss, the controller (kd or kp) is the next lever, not geometry.
notes: Integrator package for the iteration 3 lead with the iteration 7 spread. Only the spread differs from iteration 3, so the race isolates spread against the lead.
rationale: Iteration 7 (y=0.065 m, +/-0.065 m spread, 16 mm, radius 0.03 m) scored 35.77, below iteration 3 (51.31). Its slalom line loss returned at one event per run, and s-bend progress fell back to 0.04. Iteration 3 (y=0.07 m, +/-0.05 m) is the best design so far. Iteration 6 showed that speed 0.04 m also causes line loss, so ground speed stays at 0.03 m. Slalom steering_oscillation has stayed at 0.13 to 0.14 at every row tested (iterations 3 to 7), so it is not driven by the lead. This iteration restores the 0.07 m row and keeps the wider +/-0.065 m spread, which is the Builder's proposal. The controller is held at iteration 3 settings (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.10, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]), so the result reflects geometry only. The spread change is the only variable compared with iteration 3. If line loss stays at zero and slalom max_error falls below 0.06 m, the spread was the missing piece. If line loss returns, the 0.07 m lead itself is the trigger at this speed. Expected score is near or above 51 if line loss does not return. Risk: the wider spread may reduce signal resolution near centre, which would show up as higher rms_error.
